question: Should OpenClaw adopt this RFC-level recovery lifecycle boundary, including core-owned restored admission and host-owned ingress, handoff acceptance, wake, placement, and destruction?
rationale: The branch proposes durable compatibility and operational responsibilities across OpenClaw and external hosts; source-level review cannot determine whether that is the intended permanent product contract.

options.title: Keep the RFC narrow for now
options.body: Leave RFC 0013 focused on verified SQLite artifacts and continue the scale-to-zero ownership discussion in https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/114145 before accepting a lifecycle addendum.

options.title: Sponsor the sidecar contract
options.body: Accept the proposed division as a distinct, explicitly versioned recovery-lifecycle RFC and review the linked core implementation slices against it.

options.title: Request a smaller seam
options.body: Ask for a reduced proposal limited to the minimum new OpenClaw invariant needed by hosts, leaving broader handoff and admission policy outside this RFC.

recommendation.title: Keep the RFC narrow for now
recommendation.body: Leave RFC 0013 focused on verified SQLite artifacts and continue the scale-to-zero ownership discussion in https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/114145 before accepting a lifecycle addendum.

likelyOwner.reason: The proposal is explicitly composed around the snapshot contract associated with Vincent and was directly submitted for that review context.
